title: Zoom in: a cache node joins the ring, and only its arcs change owner
caption: The ring is data pushed to every app server; the only cost of a join is one miss per moved key.

messages.label: register D, weight 1
messages.note: D boots empty and registers. It is not on the ring yet, so it gets no traffic.

messages.label: place 128 tokens for D
messages.note: hash("D#0") … hash("D#127"). Each token takes over the part of an arc between the previous token and itself.

messages.label: ring v42
messages.note: Every app server swaps in the new sorted token array in one step: no request sees half a ring.

messages.label: get product:42
messages.note: This key sits on one of D's new arcs, so it now maps to D.

messages.label: set product:42, TTL 10 min
messages.note: D warms from real traffic. Keys outside D's arcs never moved and still hit on C and the others.

scenarios.name: Warm before going live
scenarios.summary: No miss spike, at the price of a dual-read window and more client logic.

messages.label: ring v42 (D shadow)
messages.note: App servers learn D's future arcs but keep reading from the current owner.

messages.label: copy product:42
messages.note: Hits on keys that will move are copied to D in the background.

messages.label: ring v43 (D live)
messages.note: After a few minutes D holds most of its hot keys; flip it live.

scenarios.name: Graceful leave
scenarios.summary: Removing a node is a join in reverse: its arcs merge into the next tokens, and only its keys miss.

messages.label: ring v44 without C
messages.note: C's tokens are deleted; each of its arcs now belongs to the next token clockwise.

messages.label: get product:42
messages.note: The key's next owner happens to be D.

messages.label: terminate C
messages.note: Only once no app server still runs a ring that includes C.

scenarios.name: D dies during the join
scenarios.summary: Treat a timeout as a miss and let health checks take D out; its arcs return to owners that still hold most of those keys.

messages.label: get product:42
messages.note: D's process crashed after registering. The call hangs until the 20 ms timeout.

messages.label: read product:42
messages.note: Fallback: serve from the DB rather than fail the page.

messages.label: ring v43 without D
messages.note: Health checks fail; D is removed and its arcs go back to their previous owners, whose old entries are mostly still cached.
